title: Same 200 day filter on both: QQQ made 87.6% and TQQQ made 41.5% with twice the drawdown
author: person-person12
selftext:
The standard answer to holding a 3x fund is that you dont hold it naked, you hold it while price is above the 200 day moving average and you step aside below it. i have never seen the 1x and the 3x run side by side on that exact rule, so i ran it twice and changed nothing but the ticker.

The rule both times: buy at the close the day price closes above its 200 day simple average, sell at the close the day it closes back below. No stop, no target, the average is the only exit. Daily candles, January 2019 to the end of March 2026, ten grand each, commission and slippage charged on both sides of every trade. i ran both in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) on its own split adjusted history.

**QQQ:**

* 40 trades, 40% green
* profit factor 2.53
* ten grand to **$18,762**, up 87.6%
* worst drawdown 26.4%

**TQQQ:**

* 49 trades, 34.7% green
* profit factor 1.25
* ten grand to **$14,150**, up 41.5%
* worst drawdown **54.4%**

So on the identical rule the 3x fund finished with less than half the gain of the 1x fund and **twice the drawdown**, which means paying for 3x bought nothing here.

You can see where it goes in the trade count. The filter fired 49 times on TQQQ against 40 on QQQ, because a 3x fund crosses its own average more often than the index crosses its, and that average is drawn on a price series that moves three times as hard in both directions. Every extra crossing is a whipsaw where you sell the dip and buy back higher, and on a 3x fund each of those round trips costs three times what the same one costs on QQQ. 34.7% of the TQQQ trades finished green against 40% on QQQ, and its losers were the bigger ones.

Two things cut against this and id want somebody to raise them if it was my result. 2019 to 2026 is a single window with one serious drawdown in it, and a rule that gets whipsawed is exactly the kind whose result swings on the start date, so this is not a statement about every window. And the 200 day is the slowest filter anybody uses for this, so the faster ones people actually run, the 50 day, the 20 day, some crossover of the two, are untested by this and could land anywhere.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Drag is the explanation, yea. The post was about the size of it, because the 200 day filter gets quoted as the fix for drag and it took 46 points off the return instead.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body:
Good that you flagged the single-window caveat. Two things I'd change to isolate what's going on. First, run TQQQ with the signal taken from QQQ's 200-day average, not its own. TQQQ's own series is three times as jumpy, so it crosses its average more often, which explains part of the extra trades. Using QQQ's signal on TQQQ separates "the filter" from "the instrument," and probably narrows the whipsaw gap. Second, show buy and hold for both over the same dates, since the filter's value only shows up against that, and report time in the market, because a lower drawdown can partly reflect just being out more.

Start-date sensitivity is the other test I'd add: run it from many start dates (each month from 2010 or earlier, if you can get TQQQ's synthetic or QQQ-based history) and show the spread of outcomes. A rule that whipsaws can look very different depending on the starting point. Volatility decay in the 3x fund will also matter more in choppy stretches, so it's worth splitting results by trending versus choppy years.

If you want to see whether the whipsaws cluster, tag the losing round trips near big scheduled events like CPI and FOMC. Cymetica's EventTrader has pre-tagged event timing for that.

Did the 40% and 34.7% win rates include the slippage on the 3x fund's wider spreads?

replies.author: Both_Yoghurt1437
replies.body: Good callout, I personally use NDX indicators for all my TQQQ/SQQQ trades

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body:
Taking the signal off QQQ and applying it to TQQQ is the right test and i should have run it that way the first time. **The version i posted conflates the filter with the instrument** and you've put your finger on exactly where the extra trades come from.

Time in market is a fair hit too. A lower drawdown that comes from being flat half the year isnt the filter doing anything clever, and i didnt report it.

So i'll rerun it three ways, QQQ signal on QQQ, QQQ signal on TQQQ, TQQQ signal on TQQQ, with buy and hold and time in market beside all three. Start date sensitivity i'll do as a rolling start every month rather than one window, because one start date is how you end up arguing about a result that was a calendar accident.
